title: Lost Before Morning
description: An archive of dreams, born from the fear of forgetting and the quiet envy of those who remember.
Embroidered into fabric, my dreams become unforgettable, a small part of the body that carries them. They’re as slow as knitting, gently resisting the speed of forgetting.
A dreamscape created to hold what would otherwise be lost before morning.

title: Split myself in two
description: Safe space. Checks. It is an intimate reflection of my comfort zone. My safe space within the fashion world.

Through this collection, I want to create a safe environment, a cocoon that protects us from this world and from others. By exaggerating everything to the extreme, the designs feel protective and reveal little of what lies beneath.
A shield. A coat. A catsuit. A silhouette without details of what must be protected. A second skin. A subtle barrier.

studies.title: Study of the Dress
studies.description: Tartan, rebellion, and the raw beauty of imperfection. Inspired by Vivienne Westwood and the Scottish punk movement, where identity was loud and proud. It's about pride, rebellion, and the freedom to take up space. The shape is exaggerated, the stance strong. A tribute to individuality, to dressing as an act of resistance and pride.

studies.title: Paper Study
studies.description: Inspired by Día de los Muertos, where life and death meet in color. Not as an ending, but as a continuation of life. The flowers, bright and fragile, became a symbol of memory and rebirth. It's a reflection on remembrance and renewal. Through layers of soft, pleated paper, I explored how something delicate can still carry meaning, how remembering can be both light and heavy at once. The layers echo the softness of flowers — fragile, temporary, yet full of life. It's a reflection on remembrance and renewal. Paper becomes a skin for memory, light enough to breathe, strong enough to hold what has passed.

studies.title: Recycled Denim
studies.description: This work started from my thoughts about homelessness, about what it means to have, or not have, a place to feel safe. To build something protective out of what is usually thrown away: recycled denim, plastic and an old sleeping bag. Each material holds traces of use, of care, of survival. It's about warmth, dignity, and the quiet wish for a softer world.
